tw-ia-barnum-barner-farm-1914.st: The scheme was run by George Rentz, his son Frank and Collins, a jeweller of Wells, Minn.; about $7,000 was recovered, plus eleven trunks in storage at Fort Dodge, inventoried for creditors.
src: Webster City Freeman, 9 Jun 1914, p. 1, from the Fort Dodge Chronicle (newspapers.com 143684695)

set.tovw: Hint only; house searched 1907, nothing; no spot
set.st: Herman Ludtke, about 70, a Grundy Center music teacher for 29 years, died at the county poor farm in Aug 1907. He had hinted at 'considerable money stored away' and had received $600 from Germany two years before; a committee searched his house and found nothing. 'Possibly he has wealth buried somewhere in the county.' No spot named. Pin is the town, not a spot.
set.t: Hint only; no spot. Urban: look-only.

src: Marshalltown Evening Times-Republican, 24 Aug 1907, p. 3 'Died of Broken Spirit' (newspapers.com 352739099)
